fields.System.Title: CNT-1 — Count planning
fields.System.Description:
Purpose

Decide what gets counted, how often, and why — so counting effort goes where it changes the
accuracy number.

Scope

In. Count plans, ABC classification, scheduling, event-triggered counts.

Out. The counting itself — that is [CNT-2](CNT-2-counting.md).

Design notes

Four trigger types, and they answer different questions.

| Trigger | Question it answers |
|---|---|
| ABC schedule | Is our accuracy holding on the stock that matters? |
| Zero pick | Why did that location say it had stock? |
| Random sample | Is our accuracy figure itself honest? |
| Targeted | A supervisor suspects something |

CNT-104 is the highest-value story here. A zero pick is direct evidence that a location's
record is wrong. Counting it immediately catches the error while the cause is still traceable,
instead of waiting for its scheduled turn months later.

Do not schedule a count for a location with open tasks. It is a guaranteed variance, and it
teaches people that variances are meaningless.

Risks

| Risk | Reference |
|---|---|
| Counting a location with open tasks | [doc 09 §6.5](../../../docs/09-defect-hotspots.md) |
| Count plan too ambitious for the staff available | [doc 05 WF 10](../../../docs/05-workflows.md) |
